project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan crash against the staged ARVO checkout `eb2d1e6ddfbdece4a52dc0c59cc7e70ba9447990`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `66d9839e994bacee374b4c2d8f487a5a647e7d2d`. This staged checkout is the merge-base ancestor of both metadata commits and already contains the same vulnerable `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` ownership bug plus the same fix hunk shown in `patch.diff`, so all line anchors below use the staged checkout's exact line map.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42508603 (gpac): Heap-use-after-free READ 8 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42508603
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: The exact 65-byte witness begins `00 00 00 00 6d 70 34 61`, so the root box is a zero-sized `mp4a`. Its remaining 29-byte sample-entry payload starts at byte `0x24` with `00 00 00 15 77 61 76 65`, a `wave` box of size `0x15`. Inside that `wave`, bytes `0x2c-0x33` are a nested `esds` header, bytes `0x34-0x37` are the nested full-box version/flags, and byte `0x38` is one extra `0x20` still inside the 21-byte `wave` box; bytes `0x39-0x40` are eight more `0x20` bytes that remain after `wave` inside `mp4a`. In the staged checkout `eb2d1e6ddfbdece4a52dc0c59cc7e70ba9447990`, `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()` first keeps the parsed `GF_ESDBox` in the registered `wave` box's `child_boxes`, and `audio_sample_entry_on_child_box()` then takes the `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` arm for `mp4a`, routes configuration handling to `ptr->esd`, and aliases that same nested `esds` object into `ptr->esd` without moving it out of the wave child list. The byte at `0x38` only triggers the saved `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes` warning inside `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` and is skipped; the normal parse fails later because `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()` then tries to parse a second child from the trailing eight bytes at `0x39-0x40` and returns nonzero. `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` therefore rewinds, raw-scans the same 29-byte payload, matches the nested `esds` header at raw-buffer offset `i=8`, and calls `gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, (GF_Box *)ptr->esd)`. Because the aliased box is still owned by the registered `wave` box's nested `child_boxes`, that helper frees the old `GF_ESDBox` without clearing the stale nested-list reference. Later movie teardown walks the surviving nested entry, passes the freed pointer back into `gf_isom_box_del()`, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1803`. The staged patch resolves this exact obligation by unlinking the old `ptr->esd` from `ptr->child_boxes` and from each surviving direct child's `child_boxes` before deleting it.

source.description: The registered `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` child path walks the parsed wave box's nested children and aliases the nested `esds` object into `ptr->esd`.
source.value_from: In the exact witness, bytes `0x24-0x37` are `00 00 00 15 77 61 76 65 00 00 00 0c 65 73 64 73`, so the remaining `mp4a` payload is a registered `wave` box whose first nested child box is `esds`.
source.note: This staged tree reaches the `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` arm, not the `GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_UNKNOWN`/`original_4cc` fallback. The nested `esds` already exists under the wave box's child list when this alias is created.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. During recursive teardown, `a` is the freed old `GF_ESDBox *` still stored in the registered `wave` box's nested `child_boxes` list, so this read dereferences freed heap memory.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 8` at `/src/gpac/src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1803:19` in `gf_isom_box_del`, reached from `gf_isom_box_array_reset()` during `gf_isom_delete_movie()`.

root_cause.description: Fallback ESDS reparsing deletes the old aliased `ptr->esd` through the audio sample entry's direct `child_boxes` list even though the registered `wave` child still owns that same object in its nested `child_boxes` list.
root_cause.note: The staged patch replaces this single delete call with explicit unlinking from `ptr->child_boxes` and from each direct child's `child_boxes` before `gf_isom_box_del((GF_Box *)ptr->esd)`, confirming that the missing obligation was to clear every surviving parent-list reference before freeing the old ESDS box.

tainted_value_origin.description: For an `mp4a` parent, the registered `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` handler routes the witness's nested configuration box into `ptr->esd` and expects that configuration to be an `esds` child.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The witness bytes `00 00 00 15 77 61 76 65 00 00 00 0c 65 73 64 73` decode as a registered `wave` box whose first nested child is `esds`, so this arm selects `ptr->esd`/`ESDS` as the target pair.

parser_admitted.description: After the top-level zero-sized `mp4a` box is accepted and the sample-entry header is consumed, GPAC enters the audio sample entry child-box parser. The saved run log proves this exact path by reporting `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes` from this function.

evidence_limitations: The staged source snapshot is checkout `eb2d1e6ddfbdece4a52dc0c59cc7e70ba9447990`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `66d9839e994bacee374b4c2d8f487a5a647e7d2d`; however Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan crash against this staged tree, and the staged `patch.diff` fixes the same ownership bug there.

Runtime disambiguation remained disabled (`run_flags.json` has `runtime_disambiguation: false`), so no extra instrumentation was added. The ownership chain above is closed from the staged source, the saved ASan allocation/free/crash stacks, the witness bytes in `poc`, and the patch hunk.

fine_trace.note: While parsing the witness's nested `esds` box inside the `wave` payload, GPAC allocates a new `GF_ESDBox`. The saved ASan allocation stack identifies this constructor as the heap origin of the object later freed and re-read.

While parsing the registered `wave` box's payload under the outer `mp4a` sample entry, the generic box-array reader creates that wave box's `child_boxes` list and adds the newly parsed ESDS object to it. This is the owning nested-list reference that later survives the free.

The root box header `6d703461` makes `s->type == GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_MP4A` on this path, so in the `GF_QT_BOX_TYPE_WAVE` case the handler chooses `ptr->esd` as the destination field and expects the nested configuration box type to be `esds`. This maps the witness's registered wave child onto the audio entry's ESD slot.
fine_trace.value_from: The witness bytes `0x04-0x07` are `6d 70 34 61`, so this registered `wave` child is being attached under an outer `mp4a` sample entry.

fine_trace.note: Source. The handler walks the parsed wave box's nested children, finds the `inner_box` whose type matches `ESDS`, and assigns `*cfg_ptr = inner_box`. Because step 3 bound `cfg_ptr` to `ptr->esd`, this aliases `ptr->esd` to the same heap object already stored in the wave box's child list.

On the crashing path `drop_wave` remains false, so the registered `wave` box is not removed from `ptr->child_boxes` and the old ESDS is not moved out of `a->child_boxes`. The aliased object therefore still has its owner-list reference under the nested wave box when control returns.

The normal child-box read does not fail at the `wave` warning itself. Inside `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()`, the byte at file offset `0x38` only makes `to_skip == 1`, logs `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes`, increments `unused_bytes`, and `gf_bs_skip_bytes()` consumes that byte while leaving the `wave` parse successful. Because the outer `mp4a` payload still has eight bytes left at `0x39-0x40`, `gf_isom_box_array_read_ex()` immediately attempts a second child parse from those trailing `0x20` bytes; that all-`0x20` header claims a box larger than the remaining input, so the second `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` returns nonzero. That nonzero `e`, not the warning itself, is why `audio_sample_entry_box_read()` skips `if (!e) return GF_OK;` and falls through to the raw fallback.

The fallback rewinds to `pos`, copies the same 29-byte remaining `mp4a` payload, and scans it for an `esds` header. In the exact witness this copied buffer begins with the 8-byte `wave` header, so when `i == 8` the candidate box starts 8 bytes into the buffer and `data[i+4..i+7]` (offsets 12-15) are `65 73 64 73`; that is the nested `esds` type the loop matches for reparsing.

Root cause call site. Because step 7 matched the nested `esds` header at `i=8` and `ptr->esd` still aliases the old nested box from steps 3-4, the parser asks `gf_isom_box_del_parent()` to delete that box through the audio sample entry's direct `child_boxes` list instead of the nested wave list that still owns it.

This helper only tries to remove `b` from the caller-supplied list and then unconditionally frees it. Here the caller supplied `&ptr->child_boxes`, but the surviving owner list is the nested wave box's `child_boxes`, so freeing `b` leaves that nested list entry dangling.

Later `gf_isom_delete_movie()` recursively destroys top-level boxes. When teardown reaches the registered wave box's nested `child_boxes`, `gf_list_get()` returns the freed old ESDS pointer from step 9 and passes that dangling `a` back into `gf_isom_box_del()`.
Sink. `a` is the dangling pointer retrieved in step 10, so reading `a->child_boxes` dereferences the freed `GF_ESDBox`. AddressSanitizer reports the heap-use-after-free READ 8 at this line.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports `gf_isom_box_del /src/gpac/src/isomedia/box_funcs.c:1803:19`, which is the exact `child_boxes = a->child_boxes;` read in step 11.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The object allocated by `esds_box_new()` in step 1 is added to the registered wave box's child list in step 2, routed and aliased into `ptr->esd` in steps 3-4, and then freed through `gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, ...)` in steps 8-9.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved free stack `esds_box_del -> gf_isom_box_del -> gf_isom_box_del_parent -> audio_sample_entry_box_read` matches steps 8-9, and the crash stack `gf_isom_box_del -> gf_isom_box_array_reset -> gf_isom_box_array_del -> ... -> gf_isom_delete_movie` matches steps 10-11.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact `wave`/nested-`esds` witness first stores the allocated ESDS under `wave->child_boxes` in step 2 and aliases it into `ptr->esd` in steps 3-4. The byte at `0x38` only triggers the saved `wave` warning; the fallback executes because step 6's second child-parse attempt over bytes `0x39-0x40` returns nonzero, then step 7 matches the nested `esds` header at `i=8` and steps 8-9 free the old ESDS without unlinking the wave child list, so teardown later reuses that dangling pointer at the sink.

format.name: minimal `mp4a` root box with nested `wave`/`esds` payload
format.contract: The trigger is the exact 65-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42508603/poc`. Bytes `0x00-0x07` are `00 00 00 00 6d 70 34 61`, so the root box is a zero-sized `mp4a`. Bytes `0x24-0x2b` are `00 00 00 15 77 61 76 65`, making the remaining sample-entry payload start with a 21-byte `wave` box. Inside that box, bytes `0x2c-0x33` are `00 00 00 0c 65 73 64 73` (a nested `esds` header), bytes `0x34-0x37` are the nested full-box version/flags, and byte `0x38` is the single extra `0x20` still inside `wave`. Bytes `0x39-0x40` are eight more `0x20` bytes after `wave` inside `mp4a`. On this staged source, the byte at `0x38` only produces the saved `Box "wave" (start 36) has 1 extra bytes` warning; the fallback path is taken because the next child-parse attempt over bytes `0x39-0x40` returns nonzero, after which the raw scan re-matches the nested `esds` at buffer offset `i=8` and frees a box that is still stored in `wave->child_boxes`.
